Implement **Phase 8** as specified in `docs/Vinea_ERP_Master_Plan_v5.md` §5 (P8), ADR-04 (balances are derived, never stored), ADR-05 (modules post through the PostingEngine — nothing here writes a journal line), ADR-06 (money, dated rates, base amounts frozen at posting), ADR-10 (jobs for the remittance PDFs), §6 (the invariant suite grows a banking suite), Appendix C (the owner's *Bank reconciliation* and *Cashbooks* rows under Reports → GL, tagged P8 since the tree was written) and Appendix C.2 ("bank statement import & reconciliation workspace as transactions not just reports (P8)"). P7 deferred **bank and cash revaluation** here (Master Plan, "Deferred out of P7"); it lands in decision 8.

Banking adds **no ledger and no second balance**. The cashbook balance is Σ `journal_lines` on the bank account — it has been since P2 and it stays that way; a bank statement is the bank's record of the same money, imported as it came and never edited; a *match* is the assertion that a statement line and a ledger line are the same event; a *reconciliation* is the dated proof that every statement line has its ledger line and the remainder is explained. Nothing on the statement side moves money: when the statement shows a fee the ledger lacks, the user **posts** a cashbook entry through the kernel, and then it matches. If you find yourself storing a balance, adjusting a ledger figure to meet the statement, or letting a statement line become a journal line without a posting, stop — the ledger is the truth and the statement is evidence.

Two mandatory **STOP for owner approval** gates: after step 2 and after step 5. Report and wait for an explicit go-ahead. Never continue past a report on a "Continue to iterate?" prompt. Every step starts from a pulled `main` on its own branch (`p8-step-N`); once a step is approved, the next may branch from that approved head and rebase onto `main` before its PR (the merge rhythm since P6 step 7). PR titles `feat(bank): P8 step N — …`; the owner arms auto-merge; the agent merges nothing. Every step report ends with `git status --short` and `git log @{u}..` both empty, quoted, and `git diff --stat` before any "N passed" claim. Gate steps (2, 5, 9) add their row to `docs/approvals.md` in the same PR — not after the fact. Step reports are committed as `docs/p8-step-N-report.md` on the branch and are the PR body.

Where the plan leaves a choice open, decide, implement, and list it under "Decisions worth review" in that step's report, as P1–P7 did.

## Preconditions (already built — consume, never re-implement)

- **Tenancy and auth (P1):** httpOnly cookie sessions, `CompanyMembership`, every tenant table `ENABLE` + `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` with `FOR ALL` policies carrying `WITH CHECK`, RLS linter tests, audited service calls with a real `actor`, `platform_scope()` locked to its sanctioned callers (AST scan), dev as non-superuser `vinea_app`, migrations through `MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL` only, `make migrate-check` (DDL proof only — rule 10).
- **Ledger kernel (P2):** PostingEngine is the only GL writer. `gl_accounts.is_control` + `control_type` with `ControlType.BANK` and `ControlType.CASH` (`CASHBOOK_CONTROL_TYPES` in `app/models/gl.py`) — **bank and cash accounts are already flagged**, and they are deliberately *not* in the `control_account_modules` registry: a manual journal may not touch them (`control_account_manual_posting`), and the cashbook, the subledger settlements, the maturity job and the reversal engine may. `CashbookEntry` (`app/kernel/events.py`: `cash_account_id`, `kind` receipt / payment, counterpart `CashbookLineSpec`s with an optional tax split, one derived bank line for the gross) posts a `CB-` entry through `POST /gl/cashbook-entries`; `_cashbook_specs` in `app/kernel/posting.py` is the shape. Signed lines: **a debit is positive**, so money *into* a bank account is a positive `amount` on its line — the sign the statement's *credit* column carries. `journal_lines` carry `currency_id`, `exchange_rate`, `amount` (transaction currency) and `base_amount` (frozen); `gl_accounts` carry **no currency** — a bank account's currency is a fact P8 has to record (decision 2). `period_balances` per account × period × branch × currency; `assert_ledger_invariants`; gapless `document_sequences` with `SEQUENCE_CLAIMANTS` in `app/kernel/sequences.py` (a doc type with no claimant fails `test_every_doc_type_registers_a_claimant`); `posting.module_reversal(module)`; dated `exchange_rates`; `PeriodClosed` / year-end.
- **Subledger (P4):** `partner_documents` of `kind = settlement` are the money side — `amount`, `cash_account_id` (must be a bank/cash control account: `_settlement_account` in `app/subledger/documents.py`), `instrument_type` cash / bank / cheque / mobile / other, `maturity_date` (a dated-ahead instrument books to the post-dated account and `mature_instruments()` moves it to `cash_account_id` on a `MAT-` entry — C.1.6), `reference`, `direction`, `open_amount`; `post_document()` / `reverse_document()` (reversal refused while allocated: `document_allocated`); `allocate()` / `unallocate()` in `app/subledger/allocations.py` with realized FX on the control account (the cumulative true-up) and the settlement discount from `payment_terms` (`discount_percent`, `discount_days`, `max_discount()`), both on `ALJ-` entries; `/{role}/allocations/preview`; `/{role}/documents/{id}/reverse`; the seeded transaction types `RCT` and `PMT` default to `1120`. AR/AP control accounts are subledger-only (VN007). A settlement in a foreign currency against a base-currency bank account is **allowed today** and books at the rate keyed on the document — a USD receipt into the RWF account is how a customer's USD invoice gets paid through a Rwandan bank, and P4's allocation carries the realized FX. P8 keeps that (decision 2's currency rule is one-sided).
- **Stock (P5) and Order Entry (P6):** untouched by this phase. `app/order_entry/sources.py` is the drill-key registry the GL entry page asks "what did this entry come from"; P7 registered `vat_return` and `fx_revaluation` there.
- **Fiscalization and revaluation (P7):** `FxRevalued` is real (`app/subledger/revaluation.py`, `fx_revaluations` / `fx_revaluation_lines` with `document_id` NOT NULL, `FxRevaluationRole` ar / ap / both, the `1290` / `2190` / `4410` / `6955` accounts, preview → post with the mirror dated the next day → reverse, refusals `fx_revaluation_exists` / `fx_revaluation_not_period_end` / period not open, a job kind on `run_job`). Decision 8 extends it to bank and cash accounts rather than building a second run. The P7 lesson that governs every deep test here: **a census floor the generator cannot reach is not a floor** — read `docs/p7-step-9-report.md` §C and `tests/fiscal/test_property_fiscal.py` before writing a Hypothesis machine, and put the reach counters in the nightly summary from step 2, not step 9.
- **Jobs (P4):** `app/services/jobs.py` — `jobs` table, handlers registered by kind, `run_job` on a fresh session with `set_actor` + `set_tenant`, 7-day retention, `sweep()`; statements are WeasyPrint PDF jobs. There is no worker process for jobs; `run_job` executes after the response. The remittance advices of decision 7 are jobs of this shape.
- **Frontend (P3–P7):** tokens and primitives, the Appendix C tree in `frontend/src/design/nav-tree.ts` (later phases phase-tagged; `permission` lists mean *any of*), `DocumentWorkspaceShell` + `LineGrid` (the cashbook batch at `app/(shell)/gl/cashbook-batches/new/page.tsx` is the P3 shape P8 extends), drafts keyed by draft UUID as `Idempotency-Key`, inline `field_errors`, next-intl with every string externalised, `formatMoney`, `todayIso` / `toLocalIsoDate` / `fromLocalIsoDate` / `nowIso` in `lib/format.ts` (never `toISOString()` — ESLint and `no-utc-dates.test.ts` refuse it), `frontend/src/lib/api-enums.ts` generated from the Python enums (a new enum is regenerated, never typed), `QueryState` on every listing (a refused query is never an empty state), posting preview before Post, the report pattern (`design/components/report-page.tsx`, print preview, CSV, `pdftotext` in e2e), the GL entry page resolving its source through `sources.py`, Playwright on `docker compose` with `E2E_PASSWORD` from env on a reset database (`make db-reset` → Rugari Wines E2E with an active EBM device, Kivu Traders E2E without; `ebm-sandbox` in `docker-compose.e2e.yml`; `sandboxReset()` before anything fiscal), `axe` in CI, CI split into `backend` (xdist, `-n` capped) and `frontend` (aggregate of checks + the five e2e groups; `ci-e2e-groups.test.ts` proves every spec is in exactly one group — a new spec is placed, not discovered). - **Process rules, standing:** a screen is not done until a test has opened it with data and a committed screenshot shows rows (rule 13); every screen's e2e asserts one formatted money value and one formatted quantity read off the page; every mutating endpoint has a caller under `frontend/src` or a `by design` / `GAP (<phase>)` line in `NO_UI` (`backend/tests/test_api_has_a_caller.py`) — a P8 endpoint built in steps 1–5 is registered as `GAP (P8, step N)` naming the UI step that deletes the line, and none survives step 9; every regression test is proven sensitive by reverting the fix; no measurements in code comments (PR bodies); non-gate steps run the changed specs plus the guard tests locally and CI is the record, full local suites at steps 2, 5 and 9; `make be-lint && make be-test` in the backend container (`-n 4`), the suite last and alone; specs sharing the fixture company run together in CI order on one reset DB; a frontend change re-takes the whole touched-spec set including the axe sweeps; warm the Next dev server after `make db-reset` before a full Playwright run; commit a guard before breaking it for sensitivity; `gh` hangs in the agent's shell — open PRs through the REST API with `curl`, never merge them; exact labels (`{ exact: true }`) and a loose-lookup scan against every label a step adds; PG enums are **rebuilt** (rename / recreate / retype) in a migration, never `ALTER TYPE … ADD VALUE` (P6 step 1).

## Behaviour this phase is written to

There is no external specification to pin. The reference behaviour is **Sage 200 Evolution's Cashbook and Bank Reconciliation**, which the owner keeps as the Windows reference environment: a cashbook per bank account, the reconciliation screen where cashbook lines are ticked against the paper statement to a keyed closing balance, the "Bank Manager" statement import that matches imported lines to cashbook lines and posts recurring items by rule, the Cashbook Detail report with a running balance, and the reconciliation report listing outstanding items. Three places P8 deliberately departs from it, each a decision below: an imported statement line is an **immutable record**, not an editable batch line (decision 3); a match is **n:m and must balance** — the difference is posted, never stored (decision 4); a locked reconciliation is a **snapshot that never changes**, with late lines shown beside it rather than folded into it (decision 5). Where the owner's environment answers a question this prompt does not, say what Evolution does and what you did in the step report.

The **sample statements** the phase is written to live under `backend/tests/banking/samples/` (committed at step 1: `generic-bk-rwf-sep.csv`, `generic-bk-usd-sep.csv`, `generic-bk-rwf-overlap-oct.csv` — the three files the acceptance tape imports, in the `generic` layout of decision 3) and, when the owner supplies one, `docs/banking/samples/<bank>-<yyyy-mm>.csv` with the mapping that reads it beside it as `<bank>.format.json`. A real export is imported by the tape at step 5 the moment it exists and by the DoD at step 9.

## Out of scope — do not build

camt.053 and MT940 (the plan says CSV first; the import is one parser behind one interface so the next format is a parser, not a redesign); bank APIs, open banking, and MTN MoMo / Airtel Money API integration (a mobile-money statement is a CSV like any other); cheque printing and direct debits; cash-till counts and cash-ups (P11 — a `cash` account reconciles against nothing here, it appears in the Cashbooks report and revalues); customer receipt runs, dunning and direct-debit collection (nothing on the AR side beyond what a statement line can post); cross-currency allocation (a USD invoice is still settled by a USD-denominated receipt, as P4 built it — decision 2 says how that meets a RWF statement); an opening-balance wizard (the tape opens a bank account the P2 way, with a cashbook entry from `3400 Opening Balance Suspense`); a second job framework; any change to the P4 allocation arithmetic, the P2 rounding rule or the P7 revaluation posting map (decision 8 adds a scope to the run, it does not touch what the run does for AR and AP); auto-posting from a statement (decision 4: rules suggest, a person posts); editing or deleting an imported statement line (void the statement — decision 3).

## Decisions locked for this phase — implement exactly

1. **The module boundary.** Package `app/banking/`: `accounts.py` (the master, decision 2, and the registration hook the chart of accounts calls), `formats.py` (statement column mappings, the `generic` preset, the parser — decision 3), `statements.py` (import, preview, dedup, void), `matching.py` (the rules and the match service — decision 4), `reconciliation.py` (open, figures, lock, reopen — decision 5), `payment_runs.py` (decision 7), `reports.py` (Cashbooks, the reconciliation report, the enquiry — decision 10), `remittance.py` (the PDF job); the API under `/api/v1/banking/…` in `app/api/v1/banking.py`. Bank revaluation is not here: it is a scope added to `app/subledger/revaluation.py` (decision 8), because one revaluation run is what the accountant presses at month end. **Nothing in `app/banking/` writes a journal line**: every posting it causes goes through `post_event` with a `CashbookEntry`, through `post_document()` / `reverse_document()` and `allocate()` / `unallocate()` from P4, or through the P7 revaluation service. No new `module` string reaches `journal_entries.module`; the step-2 report says so in one line and `tests/banking/test_boundary.py` proves no module under `app/banking/` imports `PostingEngine` internals or writes to `journal_entries` / `journal_lines`.

2. **Bank accounts are a master over the flagged GL accounts, and a foreign-currency one is single-currency.** `bank_accounts`: `company_id`, `gl_account_id` (unique per company; must be a `bank` or `cash` control account — `not_a_cash_account`), `kind` (`bank | cash`, copied from the control type and asserted equal to it), `code`, `name`, `currency_id`, `bank_name`, `account_number`, `account_holder`, `bank_branch`, `swift_bic` (all nullable except `currency_id`), `statement_format` JSONB (decision 3; null on a `cash` account), `is_active`, `last_reconciled_at`, `last_reconciled_balance` (the last locked reconciliation's date and statement balance — a **cache of a stored row**, verifiable and verified by `assert_bank_invariants`, never a balance of the account). **Every bank/cash control account has exactly one row.** `app/banking/accounts.py::ensure_row(db, account)` creates the row in the base currency, and `POST /gl/accounts` and the seed pack call it in the same transaction as the account for any `bank` / `cash` control type — the kernel does not import the banking package (P5's rule about `events.py` importing upward), and invariant clause 6 is what catches a path that forgets; the back-fill migration gives every existing tenant's bank/cash control accounts their rows (`code` = the GL code, `name` = the GL name, base currency, `kind` from the control type), tested the P4–P7 way in `tests/test_p8_backfill.py` against a tenant provisioned at `0026` with posted bank lines — including a USD settlement on the RWF bank account, which must survive. `currency_id` may be changed only while the GL account has no journal line (`bank_account_has_lines`). **The currency rule is one-sided:** a line on a bank account whose currency is *not* the base currency must be in that currency (`bank_account_currency_mismatch`, refused in the engine's account check and mirrored by a DB trigger raising `VN012`, the P4/P6 pattern — engine refusal for the field error, trigger for the guarantee); a line on a **base-currency** bank account may be in any currency, because that is how a USD receipt reaches a Rwandan RWF account and P4 already values it at the keyed rate. From this follows the **reconciled amount** of a ledger line — the figure the statement side sees: `amount` on a foreign-currency account, `base_amount` on a base-currency one — and the account's **book balance** at any date, Σ reconciled amounts to that date, which equals the trial balance at that date in the account's currency by construction. Both are one function, `reconciled_amount(line, bank_account)`, used by the matcher, the reconciliation, the Cashbooks report and the invariant suite; there is no second definition.

3. **Statements are the bank's record, imported as they came.** `bank_statements`: `bank_account_id`, `number` (`BST-`), `source` (`csv | manual`), `file_name`, `file_sha256` (unique per bank account among non-void statements — the same file twice is refused `statement_already_imported`; a voided statement's hash and its lines' fingerprints block nothing, so a mistaken import is voided and the file imported again), `format_snapshot` JSONB (the mapping as it was when this file was read — a later edit to the account's format must not change what a stored statement meant), `from_date` / `to_date` (the first and last value dates), `opening_balance` / `closing_balance` (keyed at import, or read from a balance column: closing = the last line's balance, opening = the first line's balance − its amount; the preview shows both and the user confirms), `line_count`, `lines_skipped`, `status` (`open | void`), `imported_by/at`. `bank_statement_lines`: `statement_id`, `bank_account_id` (denormalised so the matcher never joins for it), `line_no`, `value_date`, `booking_date` (nullable), `description`, `reference` (nullable), `amount` (**credit positive** in the account's currency — the sign convention of decision 2's ledger side), `balance_after` (nullable), `external_id` (the bank's own transaction id when the format has one; unique per bank account when present), `fingerprint` (SHA-256 over bank account, value date, amount, normalised description, reference and the **occurrence index** among identical tuples within one file — so two identical fees on one day are two lines, and the same two in an overlapping export are skipped as two), unique per bank account. Lines are **immutable** once written (trigger, the P2 way — `VN013`); a mistaken import is **voided** as a whole (`status = void`, refused while any of its lines is in a match: `statement_has_matches`), and a voided statement's lines leave every listing and every count. An **overlapping export** — the same weeks exported again with a few new days — is the normal case, not an error: lines whose fingerprint (or `external_id`) already exists are skipped and counted in `lines_skipped`; the import result says "N new, M skipped". **Formats:** `statement_format` is a column mapping — `preset` (`generic | custom`), `delimiter`, `encoding`, `header_rows`, `date_column` + `date_format` (strptime), `description_column`, `reference_column`, `amount_mode` (`debit_credit` with `debit_column` / `credit_column`, or `signed` with `amount_column` + `sign_convention` `credit_positive | debit_positive`), `balance_column`, `external_id_column`, `decimal_separator`, `thousands_separator`, `booking_date_column` — all nullable but what the mode needs. The `generic` preset reads `Date, Description, Reference, Debit, Credit, Balance` with ISO dates. A **preview** (`POST /banking/statements?preview=true`) parses the file with the account's mapping and returns the first twenty parsed rows, the opening and closing it derived, the skip count against what is already stored, and every parse error with its row number; an import with any parse error imports nothing (`statement_parse_error`, the row and column named). **Manual statements** (`source = manual`, a paper statement) are keyed line by line on the same table and take the same path from there. Import is idempotent under `Idempotency-Key` and under the file hash.

4. **A match is an assertion that balances; rules suggest, people post.** `bank_matches`: `bank_account_id`, `kind` (`auto | manual | tick | posted`), `rule` (`reference | payment_run | amount_date | posted_from_statement | manual | tick`), `reconciliation_id` (nullable — set at lock, decision 5), `matched_by/at`, `note`; members in `bank_match_statement_lines` (`match_id`, `statement_line_id`, unique on the line) and `bank_match_journal_lines` (`match_id`, `journal_line_id`, unique on the line). **A statement line is in at most one match; a journal line is in at most one match** — DB unique constraints, restated by the invariant. Every journal member is a line on the match's bank account's GL account and every statement member is a line of that bank account (`match_across_accounts` otherwise). **A match with statement members balances**: Σ statement `amount` == Σ ledger `reconciled_amount` over its members, refused otherwise (`match_unbalanced`, with the difference) — the difference is never stored, it is *posted* (below) and the posted line joins the match. A `tick` match has journal members and no statement members (decision 5's paper mode). A match is **effective at a date** when every member is dated on or before it; a receipt dated 30 September matched to a statement credit dated 2 October is *outstanding* at 30 September and reconciled at 31 October, which is what a deposit in transit is. Unmatching deletes the match and is refused once it belongs to a locked reconciliation (`reconciliation_locked`). **Auto-match** (on import, and on demand) applies, in this order, only where the candidate is unique, and never touches an existing match: (i) `reference` — a statement line whose normalised description or reference (upper-case, alphanumerics only) contains a candidate ledger line's document number or `partner_documents.reference` / `journal_entries.reference` token, equal reconciled amount, value date within ±30 days of the entry date; (ii) `payment_run` — a statement line whose text contains a posted run's number and whose amount equals the run's total, matched to **all** of that run's settlement lines (the one-to-many the bank produces — decision 7); (iii) `amount_date` — one unmatched ledger line of equal reconciled amount within ±3 calendar days of the value date, and no second candidate. Ambiguity is not a match: the workspace shows the candidates and the person chooses. **Manual match** takes any set of statement lines and ledger lines on one account that balances (a bulk deposit against three receipts, one payment against two statement lines — both directions are one operation). **Post from a statement line** is how the ledger catches up with the bank: from an unmatched line the user posts either a **cashbook entry** (`CashbookEntry`, kind from the line's sign, `cash_account_id` = the account's GL account, one counterpart line with a GL account and optional tax code, date / amount / description / reference prefilled from the line) or a **customer receipt / supplier payment** (a P4 settlement, `cash_account_id` = the account, partner chosen, unallocated — allocation is the P4 screen's business); the posting and the `posted` match (`rule = posted_from_statement`) are written **in the same transaction**, so a posted line is never left unmatched and a failed posting leaves no match. `bank_rules` per bank account (`pattern` — case-insensitive substring on the description, `kind`, `gl_account_id`, `tax_code_id`, `partner_type` / `partner_id`, `description`, `priority`) make the drawer open **prefilled** for a recurring line (the monthly fee to `6700`, interest to `4300`); they never post on their own. The engine's `not_a_cash_account` and `control_account_direct_posting` refusals are what stop a rule from targeting a control account.

5. **A reconciliation is dated, locks at zero, and never changes once locked.** `bank_reconciliations`: `bank_account_id`, `number` (`BRC-`), `reconciliation_date`, `statement_balance` (keyed, or defaulted from the latest statement line's `balance_after` on or before the date when the account's format carries a balance column), `ledger_balance`, `outstanding_total`, `difference`, `status` (`open | locked`), `high_water_line_id`, `outstanding_snapshot` JSONB, `locked_by/at`, `reopened_by/at/reason`. One open reconciliation per bank account (`reconciliation_open_exists`); its date must be after the previous locked one's (`reconciliation_date_order`); a `cash` account has none (`reconciliation_needs_bank`). **The figures**, computed by one function and shown live while the reconciliation is open: `ledger_balance` = Σ reconciled amounts of the account's lines dated on or before the date; `outstanding` = the same sum over lines not in a match effective at that date (unmatched, or matched to a statement line dated after it) — *unpresented payments* and *deposits in transit*; `unmatched_statement` = the account's non-void statement lines dated on or before the date that are in no match; `difference` = `statement_balance − (ledger_balance − outstanding)`. **Lock** (`bank:reconcile_lock`, `Idempotency-Key`) is refused while `unmatched_statement` is non-empty (`statement_lines_unmatched`, the count named) or `difference ≠ 0` (`reconciliation_difference`, the figure named); on success it stores the four figures, the outstanding items as a snapshot (line, date, number, amount), `high_water_line_id` = the greatest `journal_lines.id` on the account at that moment, assigns `reconciliation_id` to every match effective at the date that has none, and sets `bank_accounts.last_reconciled_at/balance`. **Paper mode** is the same reconciliation with `tick` matches (decision 4) and a keyed balance; the identity is the same. **Late lines:** a ledger line dated on or before a locked reconciliation's date but posted after its lock (`journal_lines.id > high_water_line_id` — the P7 late-entry pattern, membership by id) is *outstanding* in the next reconciliation and is flagged "dated inside `BRC-n`" on the workspace and the report; the locked reconciliation's stored figures do not move, and the report shows the stored figures beside a live recomputation and lists what accounts for any difference: the late lines, and lines matched or ticked since the lock. **Reopen** (`bank:reconcile_lock`, reason required, audited): only the account's **latest** locked reconciliation (`reconciliation_not_latest`); it returns to `open`, clears `reconciliation_id` on its matches (the matches stand), clears the snapshot and the account's cache back to the previous locked one. The kernel does not refuse a backdated posting to a reconciled bank account: Evolution does not either, and a refusal would push the clerk to post a cheque on the wrong date. `assert_bank_invariants` (`tests/banking/invariants.py`, asserted after every row of the tape and every step of the machine): (1) match members unique per line, on one account, all of one bank account; (2) every match with statement members balances; (3) every match assigned to a locked reconciliation was effective at its date; (4) for every locked reconciliation, recomputing `ledger_balance` over the account's lines with `id ≤ high_water_line_id` dated on or before its date, and `outstanding` over those of them in no match carrying **its** `reconciliation_id` (the assignment made at lock is the membership — a match made afterwards, effective at that date or not, belongs to a later reconciliation and must not move a locked figure), reproduces the stored figures exactly, and `statement_balance == ledger_balance − outstanding_total`; (5) no foreign-currency bank account carries a line in another currency dated on or after its row's `created_at`; (6) every bank/cash control account has exactly one `bank_accounts` row and its `kind` equals the control type; (7) `last_reconciled_at/balance` equal the latest locked row or are null; (8) for every posted payment run, Σ member settlement totals == the run total, every member carries the run's number as `reference`, every member's `cash_account_id` is the run's account, and a reversed run has every member reversed; (9) every statement line of a void statement is in no match.

6. **The Cashbooks report is the ledger, per account, with the reconciliation beside it.** Reports → GL → **Cashbooks**: per bank/cash account and date range — opening balance, then every ledger line on the account in the account's currency (date, entry number, document type, reference, description, partner, receipt / payment columns, running balance) with a *Reconciled* column carrying the `BRC-` number of the locked reconciliation its match belongs to, "matched" for a match not yet locked, and blank for outstanding — then totals and the closing balance; a **summary** mode with one row per account (opening, receipts, payments, closing in the account's currency, closing in base, last reconciled date and balance, unmatched statement lines, outstanding lines). The closing balance is asserted equal to the trial balance figure for the account at the date, in the account's currency, by the tape and by the report's own e2e — the report is a view over `journal_lines`, and this is the tie that says so. Print and CSV as P3–P7. Reports → GL → **Bank reconciliation**: over one reconciliation (open or locked) — the account, the date, *Balance per bank statement*, *Add: deposits in transit* (outstanding positive lines), *Less: unpresented payments* (outstanding negative lines), *= Adjusted bank balance*, *Balance per cashbook*, *Difference*; then the outstanding items list, the unmatched statement lines (an open one), and, on a locked one, the *Posted after lock* section from decision 5. Both rows lose their `P8` tag; they are the owner's own rows and take no C.1 entry.

7. **A payment run pays many suppliers through P4 and reconciles to the bank's one line.** `payment_runs`: `bank_account_id` (a `bank` kind — `payment_run_needs_bank`), `number` (`PYR-`, claimed at posting; there are no draft rows — the selection is previewed and posted in one call, P7's preview → post shape), `payment_date`, `currency_id` (the account's), `total`, `reference` (the run's number, stamped on every settlement it posts), `status` (`posted | reversed`), `posted_by/at`, `reversal_reason`, `idempotency_key`; `payment_run_lines`: `partner_id`, `document_id` (the AP invoice paid), `amount`, `discount_amount`, `settlement_document_id` (the `PMT-` it produced), `allocation_id`. **The reading of the plan's "batch supplier payments → single bank line":** the run posts **one settlement per supplier** through `post_document()` (kind settlement, `cash_account_id` = the account's GL account, `instrument_type = bank`, `reference` = the run number, amount = Σ of that supplier's lines net of discount) and **one allocation per supplier** through `allocate()` against the selected invoices, taking the settlement discount P4 computes when `payment_date` is inside the terms' discount window (the preview shows `discount_available` per line and takes it by default; the user may decline it per line), all in one transaction — so every payment is an ordinary P4 document with its own `PMT-` number, entry, open item and reversal, and the AP subledger sees nothing new. The **single bank line** is the statement's: a bulk transfer shows on the statement as one debit carrying the run's reference, and decision 4's `payment_run` rule matches that one line to the run's N ledger lines. A clearing account (post the N settlements to a clearing account, then one bank entry for the total) was considered and rejected: it buys a literal single ledger line at the price of an account, a control type and a kernel event, to restate a fact the bank already states — and a bank that shows one line per beneficiary would then need the reverse mapping. Record this reading in the step-3 report and the final report. **Selection:** open AP invoices (`open_amount > 0`, `kind = invoice`, in the run's currency) by supplier, due on or before a chosen date, any subset, partial amounts allowed (`payment_exceeds_open` above the open amount); a supplier with open credits (unallocated payments, returns) is listed with a warning naming them, never netted — allocation is P4's screen; a document that is not open at posting (paid meanwhile) fails the run (`document_not_open`, nothing posted — the refusals of `plan()` run before the first write, P7's rule). **Outputs:** the **instruction file** — a CSV download per run in a generic layout (`beneficiary, bank, account number, amount, currency, reference, supplier code`) read from the new `partners.bank_name`, `partners.bank_account_number`, `partners.bank_account_holder` (nullable, edited on the Suppliers screen); a supplier without bank details is listed in the run with `bank_details_missing` as a warning, and the file carries the row with the missing fields empty, because the payment was posted and the accountant needs to know which beneficiary to key by hand; a bank-specific layout is a mapping on `bank_accounts.instruction_format` when the owner supplies one (not in scope until then). And the **remittance advice** per supplier — a WeasyPrint PDF job (`remittance_pdf`, the statement-job shape: bytes in the row, 7-day retention) listing the invoices paid, discounts taken and the payment. **Reversal** (`bank:payment_run_post`, reason required): unallocates every allocation and reverses every settlement, in one transaction, **fallible leg first** — `unallocate()` for each line, then `reverse_document()` for each settlement (which refuses `document_allocated` if any allocation survived, which is the proof the order is right), then the run is `reversed`; a member settlement reversed on its own from `/ap/documents/{id}` is refused `payment_run_member` ("reverse the run"), because a bulk transfer is one banking act and the bank will show one line either way. A run whose statement line is already matched is reversible — the reversal releases the match (the statement line is unmatched again, and the reversing entries are outstanding until the bank returns the money or the accountant posts what happened) — and a run inside a *locked* reconciliation is not (`reconciliation_locked`; reopen it first, decision 5).

8. **Bank and cash revaluation is a scope of the P7 run.** `FxRevaluationRole` gains `bank` (every active `bank_accounts` row whose currency is not the base) and `all` (`ar` + `ap` + `bank` — the month-end press); `both` stays for stored rows. The enum is rebuilt in the migration (rename / recreate / retype). `fx_revaluation_lines.document_id` becomes nullable and the table gains `bank_account_id` (nullable) with a CHECK that exactly one of the two is set; a bank line carries `currency_id`, `open_amount` = the account's book balance in its currency at the date (Σ `amount`), `carrying_base` = Σ `base_amount` at the date, `rate_at_date`, `revalued_base` = `open_amount × rate`, half-up to base decimals, `difference` = revalued − carrying (`booking_rate` is `carrying_base ÷ open_amount` when the balance is non-zero, else null — it is informational on a bank line). **Posting map**, one entry per run as P7: per bank account, the gain to `4410 Unrealized Foreign Exchange Gain` / the loss to `6955 Unrealized Foreign Exchange Loss` and the other side to a new plain asset account **`1130 Bank Revaluation`** (`gl_settings.bank_revaluation_account_id`) — **never the bank account itself**, because a base-only line on a bank account (zero `amount`, non-zero `base_amount`) would be a ledger line the statement can never show and the reconciliation would carry forever; the balance sheet reads `1121 + 1130` exactly as it reads `1200 + 1290`. Lines carry no partner. The mirror the next day, the preview, `fx_revaluation_not_period_end`, the period check and the reversal are P7's, unchanged. **Overlap:** `fx_revaluation_exists` is now a scope test — each role covers a set (`ar → {ar}`, `ap → {ap}`, `both → {ar, ap}`, `bank → {bank}`, `all → {ar, ap, bank}`) and a run is refused when its set intersects a posted run's at the same date; the P7 test for the refusal is extended, not replaced. The FX revaluation screen (P7 step 7) and report (P7 step 8) gain the role and the bank lines; `assert_subledger_invariants` still holds after every bank run (it never touched the control accounts and it still does not).

9. **Settings, seed, back-fill.** New `gl_settings` keys: `bank_revaluation_account_id`, `bank_charges_account_id` (the default counterpart when a statement debit is posted as a fee — `6700 Bank Charges`), `bank_interest_account_id` (`4300 Other Income`). Seed account `1130 Bank Revaluation` (asset, under `1100`, postable, plain). `partners` gains `bank_name`, `bank_account_number`, `bank_account_holder`. Rwanda seed pack plus the back-fill migration for existing tenants (`tests/test_p8_backfill.py`: provision at `0026` with posted bank lines and a USD settlement on the RWF bank account, upgrade, assert every key and account lands non-null, every bank/cash control account has its row in the base currency, nothing posted changed, and the P7 revaluation rows still read). The Defaults screen edits the three keys; no second settings store. The e2e seed gives Rugari Wines E2E a second bank account **`1121 Bank Account USD`** (`bank`, USD) beside `1120`, and Kivu Traders none but the seeded pair — one company with a foreign-currency bank account and one without, so every screen is exercised both ways.

10. **Enquiries and drill.** Enquiries → GL → **Bank account enquiry**: per account — the book balance (currency and base), the last locked reconciliation (number, date, statement balance), unmatched statement lines (count, Σ), outstanding ledger lines (count, Σ), the latest statement imported (number, to-date), the open reconciliation if any, each figure a link into the workspace or the report. The **GL entry page** shows, on every line that sits on a bank account, its match and the `BRC-` it was locked in, or *outstanding* — `sources.py` gains nothing (no P8 posting has a document of its own to resolve to; a `PMT-` posted by a run resolves to its partner document as it does today, and the run is reached from that document's detail, which gains a "Paid in run PYR-n" link). Every listing and report sits behind `QueryState`.

11. **Permissions, numbering, idempotency, events.** New constants: `bank:setup_manage` (bank accounts, formats, rules), `bank:statement_import` (import, void, manual lines), `bank:reconcile` (match, unmatch, tick, auto-match, post from a statement line — which also requires the permission of the thing posted: `gl:journal_post` for a cashbook entry, `ar:transactions_post` / `ap:transactions_post` for a settlement), `bank:reconcile_lock` (open, lock, reopen), `bank:payment_run_post` (preview, post, reverse, the file and the advices), `bank:reports_view` (Cashbooks, the reconciliation report, the enquiry, the statement and run listings). Back-fill Administrator with all six, Accountant with all but `bank:setup_manage`, Clerk with `bank:reports_view` — the e2e seed's read-only member proves the gates are real. `DocType` entries `BST` (`BST-`, claimant `bank_statements`), `BRC` (`BRC-`, claimant `bank_reconciliations`), `PYR` (`PYR-`, claimant `payment_runs` — every row holds its number, including reversed ones, as orders do), each in `DEFAULT_PREFIXES` and `SEQUENCE_CLAIMANTS`. `Idempotency-Key` on statement import, reconciliation open / lock / reopen, run post / reverse, and every posting the workspace causes (existing on document posts). **Events: none new.** Every posting this phase causes is a `CashbookEntry`, a `PartnerDocumentPosted`, an `AllocationPosted` or an `FxRevalued`; say so in `events.py`'s comment block where the stubs were, as P6 and P7 did.

12. **The state machine and the census.** The deep Hypothesis machine for this phase (`tests/banking/test_property_banking.py`, marked `slow`, run at 300 examples on the deep profile, the reach counters in the nightly summary): random sequences over two bank accounts (one base, one foreign) and one cash account — cashbook entries, receipts and payments (some in USD against the RWF account, some dated ahead and matured), statement imports **generated from the ledger** and then perturbed (lines dropped → outstanding; lines added → post-from-statement; value dates shifted across the reconciliation date → deposits in transit; the same file re-imported; an overlapping export), auto-match, manual n:m matches, ticks, locks, reopens, payment runs and their reversals, revaluations with the mirror — at a 0-dp and a 2-dp base, asserting `assert_ledger_invariants`, `assert_subledger_invariants` and `assert_bank_invariants` after every step. `REQUIRED_REFUSALS` floors, each ≥ 3 at the deep profile: `reconciliation_difference`, `statement_lines_unmatched`, `match_unbalanced`, `reconciliation_locked`, `bank_account_currency_mismatch`, `payment_exceeds_open`, `statement_already_imported`; a floor the generator cannot reach after an honest attempt moves to a targeted property that constructs its precondition, with an anti-vacuity control, and the step-2 report names which — P7's rule, applied from the start.

## Build order — commit after each step with green checks

1. **Masters, schema, seed, formats, the parser.** Migration `0027_p8_banking`: `bank_accounts`, `bank_statements`, `bank_statement_lines` (immutability trigger `VN013`), `bank_rules`, `bank_matches` + the two member tables, `bank_reconciliations`, `payment_runs` + `payment_run_lines`; `partners` bank-detail columns; `fx_revaluation_lines.document_id` nullable + `bank_account_id` + the CHECK; `fx_revaluation_role` rebuilt with `bank` and `all`; the three `gl_settings` keys; seed `1130`; the back-fill with `tests/test_p8_backfill.py`; `DocType` entries, prefixes, claimants; permissions with the role back-fill; enums exported (drift gate green). `app/banking/accounts.py` with `ensure_row` called from `POST /gl/accounts` and the seed (a `bank` / `cash` control account gets its row in the same transaction) and the currency rule — engine refusal in `posting.py`'s account check plus the `VN012` trigger, each proven sensitive on its own (disable the engine check: the trigger still refuses; disable the trigger: the engine still refuses). `formats.py`: the mapping model, the `generic` preset, the parser with row-numbered errors, the fingerprint, `tests/banking/test_formats.py` over the three sample files and a hand-built awkward one (thousands separators, `DD/MM/YYYY`, a signed amount column with `debit_positive`, a blank reference, two identical fees on one day). `statements.py`: preview, import, dedup, void. Endpoints for bank accounts, rules, statements and preview registered `GAP (P8, step 6)` / `GAP (P8, step 7)` naming the screen that deletes each. The nightly deep-profile summary on `main` read once for the P6/P7 floors and reach lines (say what it showed — the phase must not inherit a red nightly, P7 step 1's rule). Migration applies from zero, `alembic check` clean, RLS linter green.

2. **Matching, reconciliation, the invariants, the machine. STOP.** `matching.py` with the three auto rules in order, manual n:m with the balance rule, tick, unmatch and its lock refusal; post-from-statement (cashbook entry and settlement) with the match in the posting's transaction, and `bank_rules` as prefill; `reconciliation.py` with the figures function, open, lock with its two refusals and the snapshot, reopen with its refusal, late-line detection by `high_water_line_id`; `assert_bank_invariants` clauses 1–7 and 9 (8 arrives with the runs at step 3), each proven sensitive by breaking the thing it guards; `tests/banking/test_boundary.py`. The machine of decision 12 without payment runs and revaluation (they join at steps 3 and 4), census floors for the five refusals it can reach here, the reach counters in the nightly summary. Endpoints registered `GAP (P8, step 7)`. **STOP.** Report the schema, the reconciled-amount rule with the USD-on-RWF case worked through, the figures identity, the refusal table with the test that proves each sensitive, the invariant output, the census with reach lines, and the list of floors moved to targeted properties. Wait for approval before payment runs.

3. **Payment runs and supplier bank details.** Decision 7 end to end: preview (per supplier, per invoice, `discount_available`, the total, the warnings), post through `post_document()` + `allocate()` in one transaction with `plan()`-before-write refusals, the run number stamped as `reference`, the `payment_run` auto-match rule, the instruction CSV, the `remittance_pdf` job, reversal fallible-leg-first with `payment_run_member` on the document path and `reconciliation_locked` on a locked run; invariant clause 8; the machine gains `payment_run` and `reverse_run` with `payment_exceeds_open` and `document_not_open` in the census. Tests with literals: a run over three suppliers of which one takes a 2 % discount inside the window and one has no bank details; the run's three `PMT-` lines matched by one statement line; reversal restores every open item and releases the match. Endpoints registered `GAP (P8, step 7)`.

4. **Bank revaluation, the reports, the enquiry.** Decision 8: the `bank` and `all` scopes in `app/subledger/revaluation.py`, the bank lines, `1130`, the scope overlap refusal, the mirror and the reversal under the existing tests plus new ones with literals (a USD account at 495.00 carried at 653 400 revalued at 1 350 → 14 850, the balance sheet reading `1121 + 1130 == 495 × 1 350`); decision 6's Cashbooks query (detail and summary, the trial-balance tie asserted), the reconciliation report query (stored beside live, late lines listed); decision 10's enquiry. The machine gains `revalue` and `reverse_revaluation`. Endpoints registered `GAP (P8, step 8)`.

5. **Listings, and the acceptance tape — backend. STOP.** Statement listing per account with counts and status; statement detail with its lines and their match state; the ledger-line listing per account with match state (the workspace's right pane); reconciliation listing and detail (figures, outstanding, unmatched, late lines); payment-run listing and detail; the rule listing. ## Definition of Done (all must be true)

The acceptance tape reproduces every expected value above to the rounding rule; `assert_bank_invariants` passes, so every match balances, no line is in two matches, every locked reconciliation's stored figures are reproduced from the lines that existed when it locked, and every bank/cash control account has exactly one master row; a real bank CSV (or, if precondition (d) was never held, the three committed samples) imports through a mapping, previews before it writes, skips what it already holds, and refuses the same file twice; the reconciliation reaches a **zero unreconciled difference** and **locks**, and cannot lock at anything else; a fee the ledger lacked is posted from the statement side through the kernel and matched in the same transaction; a payment run pays three suppliers through P4's settlement and allocation services, takes the discount P4 computes, produces the instruction file and the remittance advices, matches the bank's one line to its three ledger lines, and reverses as a unit with the fallible leg first; a foreign-currency bank account holds only its currency, a base-currency one reconciles a USD receipt at its base amount, and the month-end revaluation carries the bank balance to the rate of the day in `1130` without ever writing to the bank account; the Cashbooks closing balance equals the trial balance for the account at the date; nothing writes to the ledger outside the PostingEngine; every audited call passes a real actor; every mutating endpoint has a caller and the register carries no P8 line; every P8 row — Bank accounts, Bank statements, Bank reconciliation, Payment runs, Bank account enquiry, the Bank reconciliation and Cashbooks reports — is live, untagged, opened by a test with data and shown in a committed screenshot; CI green on backend and frontend. Final report: what landed, the five screenshots of step 9, decisions worth review, the state of the real-export precondition, and any plan deviations with reasons.
